QuestionStmt.S: When a ceiling fan is switched off, its angular velocity falls to $\frac{1}{3}^{\text{rd}}$ while it makes 24 rotations. How many more rotations will it make before coming to rest?

Solution.S:
Let initial angular velocity be $\omega_0$. After 24 rotations, angular velocity becomes $\frac{\omega_0}{3}$.

Using equation of motion for constant angular deceleration $\alpha$:
$$\omega^2 = \omega_0^2 - 2\alpha \theta$$
where $\theta = 24 \times 2\pi$ rad (24 rotations).

$$\left(\frac{\omega_0}{3}\right)^2 = \omega_0^2 - 2\alpha (48\pi)$$
$$\frac{\omega_0^2}{9} = \omega_0^2 - 96\pi \alpha$$
$$96\pi \alpha = \omega_0^2 - \frac{\omega_0^2}{9} = \frac{8\omega_0^2}{9}$$
$$\alpha = \frac{8\omega_0^2}{9 \times 96\pi} = \frac{\omega_0^2}{108\pi}$$

Now for the remaining motion: initial angular velocity $\frac{\omega_0}{3}$, final $0$:
$$0 = \left(\frac{\omega_0}{3}\right)^2 - 2\alpha \theta_2$$
$$\theta_2 = \frac{(\omega_0^2/9)}{2\alpha} = \frac{\omega_0^2/9}{2 \times (\omega_0^2 / 108\pi)} = \frac{\omega_0^2}{9} \times \frac{108\pi}{2\omega_0^2}$$
$$\theta_2 = \frac{108\pi}{18} = 6\pi \text{ rad}$$

In rotations: $\theta_2 = \frac{6\pi}{2\pi} = 3$ rotations.

Thus, it will make 3 more rotations before coming to rest.

Correct option: A
